item.title: West Virginia state auditor indicted over alleged scheme to take nine properties for friend
item.description: Mark A. Hunt, the West Virginia State Auditor, has been indicted by a federal grand jury on serious theft allegations. Prosecutors assert that he exploited his role to arrange property transfers for a friend, disregarding staff objections. Additionally, two senior officials from his office face charges for falsifying timecards and committing fraud. If convicted, the theft charges could lead to extensive prison sentences.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: From stage gowns to handwritten scripts: Reba McEntire opens five decades of personal archive for Nashville charity auction
item.description: Nashville buzzed recently as Reba McEntire hosted a heartfelt auction, showcasing personal artifacts from her illustrious career in entertainment. This initiative aimed to benefit the Reba McEntire Fund, assisting various nonprofit causes. Fans had the chance to bid on treasured stage outfits, scripts from her sitcom, and memorabilia celebrating her remarkable contributions to music and television. All proceeds will support initiatives dedicated to family well-being and fostering opportunities for youth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wisconsin couple sues HOA and 55 neighbours over unpaid settlement
item.description: Homeowners Lisa and Michael Newman have taken legal action against their homeowners association over outstanding settlement fees. Their previous lawsuit focused on the need for a safety fence due to their children's special needs. As part of a $200,000 settlement, other homeowners were required to contribute, but many have refused to comply, creating ongoing disputes and leave neighbors anxious about financial responsibilities.

item.title: Nvidia in crisis, AI boom at a crossroads: The tech industry's tn-dollar bet put to test
item.description: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang recently stepped down, leading to scrutiny around corporate leadership and national security. Reports regarding his personal and professional connections have intensified discussions about the company's future. Concerns have emerged about the sustainability of AI infrastructure investments across the tech industry. Many companies are reassessing their reliance on Nvidia's advanced chip technology and associated systems.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: New York mother challenges father's placement after domestic violence; appeals court orders review
item.description: A New York Appeals Court reversed a custody ruling due to inadequate consideration of domestic violence. The court emphasized the need for a comprehensive review of factors impacting children's welfare. The Family Court had failed to provide sufficient explanations regarding credibility and factual findings. Parents Edward Castro and Ashley Hawkins will have their case reassessed for custody. Current custody arrangements remain until a new evaluation takes place.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: At 8, she built 3 AI apps and taught all 30 classmates to use the technology creatively; now wins STEM award as youngest finalist
item.description: Eight-year-old Abigail Watt has developed three innovative AI applications and shared her knowledge with her peers. Her exceptional work earned her the Future Force in STEM award at the Overt STEM Awards, making her both the youngest finalist and winner. This prestigious event celebrated groundbreaking projects from the Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor, highlighting contributions from education, research, and mentorship in STEM.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mangrove forests are growing back, offering new hope for climate action
item.description: Researchers from Tulane University have observed a significant recovery in mangrove forests worldwide and their role in climate mitigation. After significant losses from 1984 to 2010, net gains have emerged since then due to natural regeneration and restoration efforts. Coastal areas are experiencing this recovery, particularly in regions like the Mississippi River Delta. Healthy mangrove forests can mitigate climate change by accumulating carbon and protecting coastlines.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed plan GTA 6 streams before its official US release: Here's what we know
item.description: Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed have announced their plans to stream Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 18. Cenat will begin his livestream at 8 PM ET, while Speed will start one hour later at 9 PM ET. The game is officially releasing in the US at midnight ET on November 19. This timing raises questions on how both streamers will access the game early.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Sozcu TV Raid: Authorities detain executives, install trustees; press freedom concerns grow
item.description: In a dramatic turn of events, Turkish authorities stormed Sozcu TV's headquarters, taking several executives into custody. This raid follows the earlier seizure of Halk TV amidst ongoing corruption probes. Observers criticize these actions as a sign of escalating political repression targeting independent media in Turkey. Following the raid, Sozcu TV's usual broadcasts were abruptly replaced with a pre-recorded segment focused on longevity.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: California school abuse case: Jury awards $29 million to former pupil who alleged teacher abused him; six more lawsuits pending
item.description: Following allegations of sexual abuse by a teacher at Luther Burbank Elementary School, a former student sought accountability through the legal system. A civil lawsuit against ABC Unified School District led to a $29 million jury award due to negligence, although the district later settled confidentially, obscuring the financial outcome. Additionally, six more lawsuits against the teacher remain active, underscoring serious concerns about how institutions manage abuse allegations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Parrot Breeding Success: Rescued pair raises two chicks; care helps birds recover
item.description: Since April 2022, the Bronx Zoo has successfully rehabilitated more than 50 parrots that were victims of wildlife trafficking. Among them, two red-lored Amazons have formed a breeding pair, successfully raising chicks in their exhibit. This achievement emphasizes the zoo's commitment to rehabilitating rescued wildlife, as they also care for white-fronted Amazons and orange-fronted conures, collaborating with authorities to further promote wildlife welfare.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: AI Spending Must Deliver Profits: Li warns bubble fears may come true; Token Exchange links AI providers with customers
item.description: Robin Li, the chairperson of Baidu, expressed his worries about a potential bubble forming in the AI sector. He pointed out that substantial investments have not yet translated into notable profit growth for businesses. Emphasizing crucial aspects of the AI domain, Li highlighted application development as vital for sustainable advancement. Baidu's new platform, Token Exchange, aims to bridge AI providers and clients efficiently.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: 100 years after Rockefeller helped save Virginia's colonial capital, $600 million plan will expand historic site and bring Constitution lessons to classrooms
item.description: Colonial Williamsburg, a historical gem revitalized by John D. Rockefeller Jr., is on the brink of a significant evolution. With an ambitious five-year plan backed by a $600 million budget, it aims to deepen understanding of American history through an expanded narrative that includes pivotal events post-independence, like the Constitution's drafting.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scotland’s beaver territories more than double since 2018
item.description: Recent findings from a comprehensive survey highlight a notable expansion of beaver territories in Tayside and the Forth regions, now totaling an estimated 405 as of 2026. The survey spanned more than 2,397 km of waterways and documented abundant beaver signs, showcasing their transition from agricultural areas to new habitats. There are ongoing efforts to support land managers in learning to live harmoniously with these wildlife populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: From 500 children in Los Angeles to 1.5M across the US: How two women built Baby2Baby into a nationwide lifeline
item.description: Baby2Baby emerged from humble beginnings in Los Angeles, aimed at delivering diapers to vulnerable children. Under the leadership of Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, it has grown to support 1.5 million children each year and distributed a staggering 850 million essential items over 15 years. Despite robust fundraising efforts, the struggle to meet the increasing demand for basic needs persists, leaving many children on waitlists.

item.title: A safe with $55,737 lay hidden in Maine woods for four years; now the mystery cash will help families stay warm this winter
item.description: A surprising find in Falmouth, Maine—$55,737 found in a safe behind the fire station—remains unclaimed. After a lengthy four-year wait for an owner, the town council has chosen to donate this money to the local LIHEAP program. This initiative promises warmth this winter, benefitting approximately 50 families as they face increasing heating costs, highlighting the community's commitment to support those in need.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shakira's foundation builds seven schools in Colombia, benefiting 5,000 children annually
item.description: In 2025, Shakira’s Fundación Pies Descalzos inaugurated seven new educational institutions in La Guajira and Tibú, benefiting around 5,000 children each year. This effort enhances the Todos al Cole initiative, which focuses on increasing school access and boosting retention rates. Furthermore, the foundation has empowered over 12,000 educators while fostering robust community networks.
